about: Arranging two windows, as a Mac's Window › Move & Resize › Arrange and Fn-Control-Shift with an arrow (docs/adr/0016-windows.mdx, decision 12): Allo's two windows (EditingProbe, its line focused, and the PressProbe companion behind it); Super+Alt+Shift with each arrow puts the active window in the first tile and the one behind it in the other, exactly, within 8 px margins at 1280 × 720, each told its size once, the active window keeping the keyboard and no key reaching either.

steps.name: Allo's first window is the active one
Super+Alt+Shift+Left: Left & Right: the active window takes the first tile, the window behind it the other; each told once, the keyboard staying in the active one
Super+Alt+Shift+Right: Right & Left: the active window takes the first tile, the window behind it the other; each told once, the keyboard staying in the active one
Super+Alt+Shift+Up: Top & Bottom: the active window takes the first tile, the window behind it the other; each told once, the keyboard staying in the active one
Super+Alt+Shift+Down: Bottom & Top: the active window takes the first tile, the window behind it the other; each told once, the keyboard staying in the active one
